# BoredMutant, full site content

> Automated client document collection for CPA firms and staffing agencies. Escalating reminders send from the firm's own mailbox and stop the moment the document arrives. No client portal, no new software for clients to learn.

## Document collection for CPA and staffing firms

URL: https://www.boredmutant.com/

**Q: Is our client data safe?**

A: Attachments never leave your inbox. The system tracks names, email addresses and document titles only. It never opens, stores or moves the files themselves. Everything sends through your own mailbox using your own credentials.

**Q: What if the AI writes something wrong to a client?**

A: It can't, because it doesn't write. You approve three fixed templates once, in your firm's voice. The system only decides when to send them and when to stop. No generated text ever reaches a client.

**Q: What happens when a client replies with a question?**

A: That client's chase pauses instantly and the thread goes to your staff, flagged for attention. The system only chases silence, so once a client has actually replied it steps back.

**Q: Do our clients need to learn new software?**

A: No. They reply to your email with the file attached, the way they always have.

**Q: How long until it's running?**

A: About a week from the call. Ten minutes of your time to hand over the list, one round of template approval, then two days in dry-run mode where you watch every email it would have sent before any real one goes out.

**Q: What if we want to stop?**

A: Cancel any time, because it's month to month. Your clients were never on a platform and your data never left your systems, so nothing needs migrating. You go back to chasing manually.

## How automated document collection works

URL: https://www.boredmutant.com/how-it-works

Home / How it works

The whole system, drawn out. There is no dashboard and no client portal. This is the actual shape of what gets installed: a scheduled workflow that reads your chase list, checks what came back, and sends the next reminder in your own words, or stops. ~1 weekFrom the first call to live, including the dry run 3 templatesWritten by you, approved once, never rewritten by the system 0 loginsNobody has an account to create, staff or client The daily run

One pass, every weekday morning. Each open item is evaluated on its own. Watch it run. The pulse follows a single document from the list to the send. Document chaser · daily pass ▶ Run the flow ◷Schedule triggerEvery weekday at 09:00 in your firm's timezone. Mon–Fri 01Read the chase listPulls every open item: client, document, deadline, current stage, date last contacted. 02Filter: what is actually due?Skips anything already received, paused by your staff, or not yet at its next step. 03Check the threadReads inbound mail on each open thread since the last run. Subject, sender, whether a file is attached, though never the contents of the file. Attachment arrived ✓Stop the sequenceItem marked received. No further mail on it, ever. Goes into Friday's digest as complete. Silence →Advance a stageMove the item to the next escalation step and continue below. Reply, but no file !Pause and hand to staffThread flagged in your inbox for a human. The system sends nothing further on that item until someone resumes it. 04Select the approved templateStage 1 polite, stage 2 firm, stage 3 final. Your wording, merged with the client name, document and deadline. 05Send from your mailboxAuthenticated as your firm. Your address, your signature, and it lands in your own Sent folder like any other email. 06Write back to the logRecords the stage, timestamp and message id, then sets when this item is next due. ↺ Repeats the next weekday until the document arrives, a human steps in, or you stop it Every item is handled independently. One client going quiet has no effect on anyone else's sequence. The weekly run

One email on Friday, and that's the reporting. Friday digest ▶ Run the flow ◷Weekly triggerFriday, late afternoon. Fri 16:00 01Aggregate the weekReceived, still outstanding, paused for a human, and what is due next week. 02Compose the digestFour short lists, in the body of one email. ✓Send to whoever should see itPartner, office manager, or both. Proof of work, every week, without asking anyone for a status update. Never writesEvery word a client reads was written and approved by your firm. The system chooses timing, not language. Files stay closedIt detects that an attachment exists. It does not open, download, store or forward it. Never over-sendsOnce a document is received, that sequence is finished. There is no fourth email. Only your listIt only contacts people on the list you handed over, about documents you listed. What's actually built

The diagram is the part that takes an afternoon. Workflow engines are a commodity, and the shape above is not where the work is. These are the parts that take a week and are specific to your firm. Mailbox layer

Sending as you, safely Authenticating against your Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace tenant with least-privilege access, threading replies correctly so conversations don't fragment, and making sure everything lands in your Sent folder rather than arriving from a stranger. Reply handling

Telling a document from a question An out-of-office is not a reply, and "sending tomorrow" is not a document. Getting this boundary right is what keeps the system from either nagging someone who already answered or going quiet on someone who didn't. State

Knowing where every item stands One record per client per document: stage, last contact, next due date, who paused it and why. This is what makes the Friday digest possible and what stops two staff members chasing the same person. Your wording

Three templates that sound like your firm Drafted with you, not for you. Firms that chase gently and firms that chase hard both work, but the escalation has to match how you actually speak to clients, or your staff will quietly turn it off. Before anything real sends Every new firm runs two full days in dry-run mode. The workflow executes exactly as above, but instead of sending, it writes each message it would have sent into a file for you to read. Nobody receives anything until you have looked at that file and said go.

## Client document collection for CPA firms

URL: https://www.boredmutant.com/document-chasing-for-accounting-firms

**Q: Will this annoy clients we've had for twenty years?**

A: Only if your templates do. The escalation is written by you and it is per-client adjustable, so long-standing clients can be set to a gentler cadence or excluded entirely. In practice most firms find the opposite problem: clients prefer a predictable reminder to a partner calling them in April.

**Q: Does it work with our practice management system?**

A: It doesn't need to. The chaser runs off a list (a CSV export, a spreadsheet, or whatever your tracker already is) and sends through your existing mailbox. If you later want it reading directly from your practice management system, that's a separate build once the chaser is earning its keep.

**Q: What happens during the busiest two weeks?**

A: Nothing different, which is the point. It does not get tired or quietly deprioritize the small clients when the large ones are loud. If anything you will want to shorten the intervals as a deadline approaches, which is a one-line change.

**Q: Who is doing this if it's one engineer?**

A: The build is one person, deliberately. It runs on your own mailbox and your own infrastructure, so it is not dependent on us continuing to exist. It is also month to month, so you are never locked into finding out.

Firms lose three to five hours per client to document collection before a single return gets started. Business returns March 15 S-corps and partnerships. This is where "we're still waiting on the client" turns into extensions you did not want to file. Extensions Sept 15 · Oct 15 The same chase, on returns everyone has already mentally closed. The easiest documents in your firm to forget about. Why timing matters Setup takes about a week, and an escalation sequence needs a head start to do anything useful. ## Document collection for staffing agencies

URL: https://www.boredmutant.com/document-chasing-for-staffing-agencies

**Q: Is chasing I-9s automatically a compliance problem?**

A: The system sends reminders and detects that a file arrived. It does not verify, complete, review or store I-9 documentation, and it makes no eligibility determination. Your existing process and your existing reviewers are unchanged; they get the paperwork sooner. We are not employment lawyers, and if your counsel wants to see exactly what sends and when, the dry-run output is a document you can hand them.

**Q: Does it work with our ATS?**

A: No. Whatever spreadsheet your coordinator actually keeps is the input, and the sends go through your existing mailbox. Reading directly from the ATS is a later conversation, once the chaser has proved itself.

**Q: Can different recruiters have different signatures?**

A: Yes. Each candidate's sequence sends under the recruiter who owns them, from that recruiter's mailbox, in their signature. To the candidate it looks exactly like the person they have been talking to all along, because it is.

**Q: What about candidates who go completely dark?**

A: After the final escalation, the item stops chasing and appears in your Friday digest as unresolved with the full contact history. That is the moment for a recruiter to make a phone call, which is what should have been happening on day eight anyway, rather than on day thirty when someone noticed.

Home / Staffing agencies

Onboarding document collection for staffing agencies. A placement is not a placement until the new hire paperwork is in. Every day a certification or an I-9 sits unsent, a start date moves and a client wonders whether you have this under control. This chases it for you, from your own mailbox, with no onboarding portal for candidates to log into. Book a 15-minute call See the workflow Where placements stall

The offer is the easy part. The onboarding paperwork is where the week goes. Unlike a tax deadline, your chase has no calendar. It is a rolling queue, one per candidate, each on its own clock. That is the kind of tracking humans are worst at. 01SourcedCandidate identified and screened. No documents needed yet. 02SubmittedClient reviewing. References and work history start getting asked for. 03 · StallOffer acceptedI-9, certifications, licenses, background consent. Everything now depends on a person who has already mentally moved on. 04 · StallOnboardingCompliance documents and client-specific forms. Missing one moves the start date. 05PlacedWorking. Now it is timesheets, weekly, forever. The expensive detail The two stalling stages happen after the candidate has said yes, which is exactly when a recruiter's attention has moved to the next requisition. Nobody is negligent; the queue is invisible unless somebody is paid to stare at it. What gets chased

Before the start date, and after it. Before the start date

One-time, and it blocks the start date Every one of these blocks a start. The escalation is short and firm because the deadline is a date somebody already promised a client. Weekly timesheetsClient sign-offExpense receiptsCertification renewalsCompliance re-attestations Renewals are just chases with a future start date. A certification expiring in ninety days becomes a sequence that begins on its own, thirty days out. Escalation can route to the recruiter, not just the candidate. The third unanswered email about an I-9 is more useful in your recruiter's inbox than in the candidate's.
